To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the mere perception of certain words, objects, or situations can automatically trigger a specific social behavior (i.e., without the person’s awareness that the behavior is being activated), and that (b) the perception of these words, objects, and situations can trigger this behavior even when it is not appropriate to do so (i.e., when it is not the best thing to do).
“Social behavior can be automatically activated by social perceptions, and that these effects occur without awareness of the causal relationship between social perceptions and behaviors.”

(1) automatic social perception influences social behavior and (2) this influence occurs through the activation of behavioral scripts that are automatically triggered when social stimuli are perceived.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the social environment influences the social behavior of individuals.
how people’s behavior is affected by the social environment in which they find themselves.
the automatic, unconscious, or nonconscious effects of social perception (e.g., stereotypes) on social behavior (e.g., aggression).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of social perception on social behavior are automatic, but not all the time.
automatic social behavior is a function of the automatic activation of social concepts.
the effects of social perception on social behavior are automatic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a number of automatic effects of social perceptions on social behaviors.
the automaticity model of social behavior is a general theory of social behavior that explains how the social mind works, how it works fast, and how it works automatically.
social perception and social behavior are in a constant interplay.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the automaticity of social behavior can have a positive effect on the quality of social interactions.
social perception and social behavior are connected in a way that goes beyond the conscious control of the individual.
people’s social perceptions and behaviors can be influenced by a wide variety of factors that they are not aware of and that they are not in control of.
